To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the processing speed of forensic tools is inadequate and the reason is that the tools are designed without considering the performance requirements.
1. Forensic processing is a real-time computation with performance requirements that are not well understood.

(1) current digital forensic software is not designed for high-throughput, low-latency processing; (2) current hardware is not designed for low-latency processing of large volumes of data; (3) there are no existing software solutions for high-throughput processing of large data sets, and (4) there are no hardware solutions for high-throughputs, low-latency data processing of large data set
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the development and validation of a new approach to forensic triage, (2) the identification and evaluation of the performance requirements for digital forensic processing, (3) the development and evaluation of a new approach for target acquisition, and (4) the identification of the performance limitations of core forensic processing functions.

the following: 1) formulating the digital forensics problem as a real-time problem; 2) identifying the core forensic functions that need to run in real-time; 3) identifying performance requirements of the core real-time functions; 4) identifying the performance requirements of the overall digital forensics workflow; 5) evaluating the suitability of existing forensic methods for real-time processing; 6) identifying the limitations of current forensic software and hardware for real-time processing, and 7

the following three questions: 1. What are the real-time performance requirements of digital forensic triage? 2. What are the performance requirements of digital forensics at large? 3. What are the intrinsic limitations of forensic software?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
digital forensics is not a real-time process, but it should be.
the current generation of digital forensic tools are inadequate for real-time triage.
, while it is not possible to process a 1 TB drive in real-time with current software, the processing speed of the average digital forensic tools can be improved significantly by a factor of 5–10.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current state-of-the-art forensic tools are not suitable for real-time processing.
the digital forensics community has not yet formulated a set of explicit requirements for performance, specifically latency.

the current generation of digital forensic tools is not capable of keeping up with the throughput of a single commodity HDD, and that a new generation of tools, based on a different set of assumptions, is needed to address this problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the average case, the forensic triage problem requires a new, more efficient, and more performant approach to digital forensics.
the digital forensic process, as it is currently practiced, is not suitable for real-time processing.
the forensic triage process should be viewed in terms of real-time computation, and we propose a new target acquisition method that enables file-centric triage.
